summary: For every 0<epsilon<=1/2, four independent Uniform[-1/2,1/2] variables X,Y,A,B give Q=2epsilon XY+2AX+2BY+2AB/epsilon=2epsilon(X+B/epsilon)(Y+A/epsilon). The slope pair has joint density cap one and the nonzero hub core tends to zero, but p_Q(t)>=(epsilon/2)log(epsilon/(2t)) for 0<t<epsilon/2, so the density is unbounded. The associated quadratic matrix has spectrum {+(epsilon+epsilon^-1),-(epsilon+epsilon^-1),0,0}; this refutes only a proposed arbitrary-remainder continuation of the r42 joint-slope method, not the three-large-eigenvalue QFORM conjecture. A valid continuation must spend genuine third curvature.
